findings.title: Missing wet-region branch in the core model-selection lemma
all_operative_hypotheses: C1 metric g and angle beta
Htan, metric C1 error and Dbeta arbitrarily small
oscillation relative to Ptheta arbitrarily small

decisive_evidence.type: Exact analytic counterexample with independent high-precision corroboration
decisive_evidence.parameters: n=1, g=Euclidean, theta=pi/3, theta0=pi/12, beta=2pi/3, VI=[Ptheta^-], S=upper wall ray
decisive_evidence.proof: The interior outward conormal is sin(theta)e1-cos(theta)e2. The upper wall conormal is -e2 weighted by cos(beta)=-cos(theta), so tangential flux cancels. Htan=Dbeta=metric error=oscillation=0. Signed density is 1/4 and negative cosine part is 1/2; total 3/4 is below 3/4+cos(pi/12)/4. V-Vtheta=-[wall]/2, hence nonzero fixed metric distance. The minimum |beta+k*pi-theta| equals pi/3. Taking a constant sequence disproves the claimed implication for every smallness threshold.

alternate_readings: Adding integer multiples of pi to beta does not change the actual signed varifold and cannot identify the two branches.
If compatible wet-region/sign normalization is imposed first, the intended branch is selected.
counterevidence: Page 40 restricts Sections 4-6 to an acute-angle normalization.
The counterexample has a smooth interior half-plane and satisfies regularity.
findings.core_dependency: Oscillation closeness -> unique signed model and angle convergence -> Theorem 6.1/7.1 reduction and first sentence of Theorem 1.11 proof.
findings.repair: State convergence to either Vtheta or Vtheta-cos(theta)[wall], or impose compatible sign and normalized angle range; explicitly normalize the branch before the main proof invokes convergence.
findings.repair_status: Missing branch and exact example proved; full replacement proof and parameter choices not certified.
findings.impact_boundary: Lemma 3.15 (3.38) and its angular conclusion are false under their written hypotheses. The opening core reduction on p54 is invalid as written. No false principal regularity theorem or whole-paper failure is established.

independent_verification.source_claim: Lemma 3.15 (3.38) and angular conclusion, pp37-38; first line of Theorem 1.11 proof p54.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: Checked n>=1 on p9, signed varifold and full metric definitions on p11, capillary Definitions 1.1/2.1, and every lemma assumption. For theta=pi/3, theta0=pi/12, beta=2pi/3, upper wet ray, all differential errors and oscillation vanish; shifted density is 3/4, below the required bound.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Computed outward conormals: interior sin(theta)e1-cos(theta)e2 and upper wall -e2 with weight -cos(theta); tangential flux cancels exactly. V-Vtheta=-[W]/2 is a nonzero signed Radon measure, hence has positive distance in (2.5). The constant sequence therefore defeats every delta for a smaller epsilon. Distance of beta+k*pi from theta has infimum pi/3. Stationarity allows both coefficient pairs (cos(theta),0) and (0,-cos(theta)).
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Example 1.3 and p40 explicitly permit wet-region swapping. The p40 acute normalization is announced for Sections 4-6; p54 still asserts the invalid convergence before its own branch treatment. Selecting the compatible sign/wet region or allowing both models addresses the demonstrated obstruction. The example is already a smooth ray; no false final regularity theorem or complete replacement proof is claimed.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Confirmed direct use in principal theorem reduction. Major is retained for the invalid core model-selection implication; the available local normalization does not make the printed implication true.

findings.title: Incorrect derivative in variable-angle first variation
all_operative_hypotheses: signed capillary varifold with integral interior
compact C1 vector fields; no density smallness required

decisive_evidence.type: Analytic product rule and opposite-sign example
decisive_evidence.parameters: n=1, Euclidean, VI=horizontal free-boundary ray, S=entire wall, beta(y)=pi/4+0.1y, phi=(1-16y^2)^2 on |y|<1/4 extended by zero
decisive_evidence.proof: For tangential fields, the horizontal ray contributes zero and the full wall integral of (cos(beta)X2)' vanishes, hence Htan=0. For compact Y=(0,phi) near the wall, actual deltaV=integral cos(beta)phi'=0.1 integral sin(beta)phi>0. The printed Hbeta=(grad sin(beta))/cos(beta)=0.1e2 produces -0.1 integral cos(beta)phi<0. The normal boundary term vanishes on Y. Correct Hbeta is grad cos(beta)/cos(beta), whose weighted L1 norm is bounded by |grad beta|.

alternate_readings: Constant beta conceals the error because both derivatives vanish.
Likely trigonometric typo still changes the asserted theorem identity for variable beta.
counterevidence: Corrected derivative retains the weighted L1 bound used by compactness and monotonicity.
The derivative vanishes almost everywhere on the zero level set of cos(beta), so weighted definition extends.
findings.core_dependency: Capillary first variation -> free-boundary mean-curvature field -> compactness/monotonicity/first-variation estimates.
findings.repair: Replace grad sin(beta) by grad cos(beta) consistently and correct the product-rule sign in Remark 3.2.
findings.repair_status: Local identity and retained weighted derivative bound proved.
findings.impact_boundary: Printed Theorem 2.2 identity false for variable beta. Subsequent small-error bounds and main regularity theorem not disproved.

independent_verification.source_claim: (2.10), printed H_beta and (2.12), p14; Theorem 2.2 second identity p15; Remark 3.2 p25.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: The definition permits a nonzero free-boundary interior ray and the full wall S=W with independently varying C1 beta. No density assumption is required for Theorem 2.2. The compact C1 nonnegative test is legitimate and its normal boundary term is zero.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Direct product rule gives delta_beta V=delta V+integral_S X dot grad(cos beta). Integration by parts for beta=pi/4+0.1y gives actual delta V(Y)=0.1 integral sin(beta)phi>0, while the printed H_beta yields -0.1 integral cos(beta)phi<0. Independently checked the function phi and its first derivative vanish at support endpoints.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Replacing grad(sin beta) with grad(cos beta) restores the exact identity. The corrected quotient is defined weighted almost everywhere, and |H_beta||cos beta|<=|grad beta|; the derivative of a C1 function is zero almost everywhere on a level set. The weighted L1 estimates used on pp26-27 survive.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained because the corrected field preserves the required small-error estimate and the checked uses; this is not a dismissal as a harmless typo.

findings.title: Cosine replaces sine in refined normal boundary flux
all_operative_hypotheses: C1 metric g and angle beta
Htan, metric error and Dbeta sufficiently small
BS is reduced wet boundary with beta not pi/2

decisive_evidence.parameters: n=1, g=Euclidean, beta=2pi/3, V=V^(beta), S=lower wall ray, alpha=1/5
decisive_evidence.proof: Model density (1+|cos beta|)/2=3/4<4/5. Errors all zero. Interior conormal eta=sin(beta)e1-cos(beta)e2. Wall conormal contribution is cos(beta)e2. Thus deltaV(Y)=sin(beta)Y1(0) and sigmaV=sin(beta)delta0=sqrt(3)/2 delta0. The printed cos(beta)delta0=-1/2 delta0 is negative and cannot equal sigmaV. Origin belongs to BS.

alternate_readings: Normal orientation is fixed to positive e1 in (2.2); reversing a convention cannot rescue the printed negative coefficient.
counterevidence: Vector identity (3.41) and tangent cone classification are consistent with the corrected coefficient.
Section 3.4 expressly is not used for the main maximum-principle/Allard argument.
findings.core_dependency: Tangent model classification -> conormal/normal scalar flux -> explicit measure identity; qualitative density classification later used in Theorem 1.19 is separate.
findings.repair: For normalized beta in (0,pi), use sin(beta) on BS and retain coefficient 1 on the free-boundary complement.
findings.repair_status: Exact model flux and local coefficient repair proved.
findings.impact_boundary: The explicit refined quantitative theorem conclusion is false as printed. Rectifiability and principal regularity are not refuted.

independent_verification.source_claim: Theorem 3.16 after (3.41), p38, and proof conclusion p40.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: For beta=2pi/3 the actual model is admissible, the reduced wet boundary contains the origin, errors vanish, and shifted density 3/4 is below 4/5. The outward normal is fixed as +e1 by (2.2).
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Recomputed interior conormal sin(beta)e1-cos(beta)e2. Adding the lower-wall endpoint flux cos(beta)e2 leaves sin(beta)e1. Thus sigma_V=sqrt(3)/2 delta_0, whereas the printed cosine coefficient would be -1/2. This contradicts a nonnegative boundary measure without any orientation ambiguity.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: For normalized beta in (0,pi), sin(beta) restores the scalar flux and is compatible with (3.41). Coefficient one on the free-boundary complement remains. Section 3.4 expressly separates this result from maximum-principle/Allard regularity; the qualitative tangent classification is not refuted.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained for the isolated explicit scalar flux error with its verified coefficient repair, without promoting it to failure of principal regularity.

findings.title: Negative wall mass undercounted in total-variation estimates
all_operative_hypotheses: Euclidean example within C1 metric class

decisive_evidence.parameters: n=1, VI=horizontal free-boundary ray, S=entire wall, cos(beta)=-9/10, alpha=1/4
decisive_evidence.proof: The full wall has no tangential boundary and the ray conormal is normal, so Htan=0. At every radius, normalized signed mass=1/2-9/10=-2/5, shifted density=1/2<=3/4, and total variation=1/2+9/10=7/5. This exceeds 7/8 from (3.11) and 1 from (3.33). The exact identity is |mu|=mu+2mu^-, whereas the bound for the interior part needs only one negative-wall compensation.

alternate_readings: If the displayed left side meant mu_VI, a single compensation would be valid; it is explicitly |mu_V|.
For positive wall weights the distinction disappears.
counterevidence: The total-variation term in the checked trace estimates needs only a uniform dimensional bound, available from Theta+2a.
findings.core_dependency: Signed density -> total-variation bound -> c delta mass errors in Lemma 3.8 and dichotomy argument.
findings.repair: Use two copies of negative wall mass for total variation, retain one copy for mu_VI, and allow a dimensional total-mass constant.
findings.repair_status: Exact measure identity and corrected uniform bound proved.
findings.impact_boundary: Specific subunit total-mass estimates fail. The regular ray example does not refute the Ahlfors or regularity conclusions.

independent_verification.hypothesis_check: The free-boundary horizontal ray plus full wall weight -9/10 is a permitted signed capillary varifold with nonzero integral interior. Htan, metric error and Dbeta vanish; shifted density is 1/2<=3/4.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Computed directly from ray length r and wall length 2r: signed normalized mass -2/5, total variation 7/5, shifted density 1/2. Hence both claimed bounds 7/8 and 1 fail. The Jordan decomposition gives |mu|=mu+2mu_minus, while interior mass needs only one compensating wall term.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Read Lemma 3.8 statement p32 and full error use p33: the affected c*delta*|mu| term needs a uniform dimensional bound, not a strictly subunit bound. Theta+2a supplies it, while the strict interior mass estimate retains one a. This separates the defective printed estimates from the unrefuted Ahlfors/rigidity conclusions.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained because the necessary downstream uniform bound and strict interior bound can both be supplied by the exact corrected mass accounting.

findings.title: Incorrect boundary-normal Taylor coefficient
all_operative_hypotheses: upward unit normal as defined in Section 2.1

decisive_evidence.type: Exact differentiation and independent difference quotients
decisive_evidence.proof: Normal first component F(t)=(cot(theta)-t)/sqrt(1+(cot(theta)-t)^2). Differentiation yields F'(0)=-sin(theta)^3. Printed coefficient cos(theta)^2 sin(theta)-1 differs by 1-sin(theta)>0. Consequently residual/t tends to a nonzero number and cannot be O(t^2).

alternate_readings: Quadratic remainder cannot hide a nonzero linear coefficient.
At theta=pi/2 coefficients agree, but the demonstrated theta=pi/3 lies in the operative non-right-angle range.
counterevidence: Correct coefficient remains strictly negative at fixed interior angles.
The homogeneous boundary Neumann condition is unchanged after correcting the coefficient.
findings.core_dependency: Normal expansion -> partial-Harnack barrier angle estimate and viscosity Neumann condition in blow-up -> excess decay.
findings.repair: Replace coefficient by -sin(theta)^3 and adjust angle-dependent barrier constants and displayed bounds.
findings.repair_status: Exact derivative and sign preservation proved.
findings.impact_boundary: Printed expansion and its reuse are invalid as written. No false limiting PDE or final regularity theorem established.

independent_verification.source_claim: Second Taylor expansion p10, (5.7) p45, boundary viscosity argument p52.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: The small slanted graph u_t(x1)=t*x1 is C2, satisfies the stated norm bound for small t, and uses the source upward normal and Euclidean metric. theta=pi/3 is away from all excluded angles.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Differentiated F(t)=(cot(theta)-t)/sqrt(1+(cot(theta)-t)^2): Fprime(0)=-(1+cot(theta)^2)^(-3/2)=-sin(theta)^3. Subtracting the printed coefficient leaves 1-sin(theta)>0, so the residual is linear and cannot enter an O(t^2) remainder.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The correct coefficient stays strictly negative for the fixed interior angle. On p52 division in the viscosity limit therefore yields the same homogeneous Neumann condition. On p45 the negative barrier term is retained with adjusted angle-dependent constants. Historical numerical difference quotients corroborate but are not needed for this proof.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained for the invalid intermediate expansion with checked preservation of the sign needed by its specific subsequent uses.
